source_fields.formulation: All arms evolve in calendar time, including unselected arms. Their fixed unknown means increase concavely in time. The learner observes only the selected arm's fresh reward and compares with the largest current mean; the variation budget is unknown.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: The reward laws $\nu_i(t)$ of the $K\ge2$ arms are fixed before interaction and evolve with absolute time, including for unpulled arms. Their means satisfy $$\mu_i(t)=\mathbb E_{X\sim\nu_i(t)}X\in[0,1],\qquad \gamma_i(t)=\mu_i(t+1)-\mu_i(t)\ge0.$$ and are discretely concave in time: $$\gamma_i(t+1)\le\gamma_i(t).$$ $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\max_{i\in[K]}\gamma_i(t)\le V,\qquad 0\le V\le K.$$

operations.query_signature: Select $I_t\in[K]$ using past observations and then observe only $X_{I_t,t}$. Rewards of other arms are not revealed. Each $X_{i,t}$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian around $\mu_i(t)$ and independent of the entire reward table before round $t$. Dependence across arms within a round does not change this feedback model. Only reward means are restricted to $[0,1]$; realizations need not lie in that interval. Causal bandit policies are allowed. Inputs $K,T,\sigma$ are public; neither $V$ nor any variation bound beyond structural feasibility is supplied. Mean functions and, for the concave model, change times are hidden. Past feedback may be reused computationally, without extra historical or sample queries beyond the explicit interface.

source_fields.complete_expression: The target is expected dynamic pseudo-regret: take the infimum over causal policies, then the supremum over fixed distribution schedules satisfying the structural and variation constraints. Expectation covers policy and reward randomness. Unknown-budget variants require one policy independent of $V$ to handle different actual variations, rather than a separately tuned known-budget algorithm for each $V$.

source_fields.runtime_guarantee: The resource budget is fixed. Expected error is not automatically converted to high probability or a random-runtime bound.
